intro: Radiation therapists deliver precise treatments and support patients through hard weeks, skills shared across imaging careers. The closest of the 25 careers below is Nuclear Medicine Technologists, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $101,370, which is 4% less than the $105,310 radiation therapists earn.
why_it_works: Each treatment means positioning patients exactly, monitoring equipment and checking in on how someone is coping. O*NET rates operations monitoring and social perceptiveness at 3.38 out of 5 for this job. Nuclear medicine, sonography and MRI use the same mix of technology and patient care. Your pay is already high, so only 5 matches pay more. The gaps are judgment and systems analysis.
tips: Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, which is 40% more, and many start as radiation therapists.
MRI technology is an 85% match and offers different schedules at similar pay.
Nuclear Power Reactor Operators earn $122,890, or 17% more, outside health care.

faq.q: What jobs can former radiation therapists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Nuclear Medicine Technologists (92%), medical sonographers (89%) and MRI technologists (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Cardiovascular technologists are 82% matched but earn $74,310, which is 29% less than the $105,310 radiation therapist median.

faq.q: Which careers for radiation therapists pay more?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more. Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470 (40% more), Commercial Pilots $123,220 (17% more) and Nuclear Power Reactor Operators $122,890 (17% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Dosimetry usually needs a bachelor's degree and certification.

faq.q: Do radiation therapists need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than radiation therapists already have, including 9 of the top 10. An associate degree is common, held by 63% of workers in the closest match, but imaging fields need their own credentials.

faq.q: What skills should radiation therapists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are judgment and decision making, operations monitoring, persuasion and systems analysis. Coordination already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so treatment planning and analysis are the main steps toward dosimetry.
